findings.title: Recheck the inclusive wall cap after child termination and receipt preparation
findings.condition: Wall time is checked only in the child polling loop. After wait4 returns, qualification/CUDA/custody receipts are read and parsed, hashes are computed, success is classified and a later inclusive elapsed time is recorded without any final wall-cap predicate.
findings.effect: SUPERVISOR_TERMINAL can say COMPLETE while its own inclusive_supervisor_wall_seconds exceeds the declared 180s CPU or 3600s real_graph cap. The disclosed unmeasured final write tail does not cover measured parsing/hash/terminal preparation before that timestamp.
findings.source_only_example: A last child-loop sample below the limit followed by delayed receipt parsing/hash preparation beyond the limit leaves cap_violation=None and success=True. No execution is needed to establish the missing predicate.
findings.required_change: In a new sealed successor, prepare receipt descriptors first, sample final inclusive elapsed immediately before final classification, mark a wall cap failure if it exceeds the fixed cap, and record that same elapsed value. Keep only the expressly disclosed final write tail outside measurement. Preserve completed/partial native work and costs.
findings.verification_requested: Use a stdlib supervisor case with controlled time below the cap at wait4 and above it after receipt preparation; require FAILED with a wall violation. Also check the within-cap completion boundary. Rebind the successor manifest and obtain fresh source review before any release.

requested_checks_reviewed: full native SAGE/NCNC epoch and candidate coverage
limits: Source review does not authorize execution or prove predictive quality.
Root-reported raw-feature prerequisite was not independently checked against its outcome receipt or payload.
Child PASS requires physical supervisor COMPLETE/custody for cap-qualified completion.
Output custody is not an asynchronous input freeze.
Only final terminal write tail is disclosed as unmeasured; B1 affects measured preparation.
